title: High-angular-resolution ALMA imaging of the inhomogeneous dynamical atmosphere of the asymptotic giant branch star W Hya: SiO, H<SUB>2</SUB>O, SO<SUB>2</SUB>, SO, HCN, AlO, AlOH, TiO, TiO<SUB>2</SUB>, and OH lines
question: What are the dynamics and chemistry in the atmosphere and inner wind (within a few stellar radii) of the asymptotic giant branch star W Hya, and how do molecular species relate to dust formation and shocks?

data.sensitivity: ~40 uJy/beam (continuum MFS); ~0.5-0.6 mJy/beam per 488 kHz channel (spectral line cubes), up to 2.7 mJy/beam in maser channels

what.value: Distance of W Hya of 98 pc

evidence.quote: In the present work, we adopted the 98 pc from Vlemmings et al. ((cite: vlemmings03))

what.value: Wind terminal velocity of 5 km s^-1 and turbulent velocity FWHM of 2 km s^-1

evidence.quote: while Hoai et al. ((cite: hoai22)) obtained, based on the analysis of ALMA data, a lower value of 5 km s$^{-1}$
In the present work, we adopted the wind terminal velocity of 5 km s$^{-1}$.
We assumed a Gaussian line profile with a FWHM of a turbulent velocity of 2 km s$^{-1}$ (Hoai et al. (cite: hoai22))

what.value: Systemic velocity of 40.4 km s^-1 LSR and circumstellar envelope gas temperature profile T_gas(r) = 2500 (2.7x10^13 / r(cm))^0.65 K

evidence.quote: As for the systemic velocity, Khouri et al. ((cite: khouri14b)) derived 40.4 km s$^{-1}$ in the local standard of rest (LSR)

evidence.quote: We adopted 41.4 mas as the star’s angular diameter (i.e., 20.7 mas as the star’s angular radius $R_{\star}$), as described in Paper I.

In the present work, we use the geometrical mean of the major and minor axis of 59.3 mas derived in Paper I as the millimeter continuum angular diameter (i.e., 29.6 mas as the continuum angular radius $R_{\rm cont}$).
The contours in Fig. [16](#integmap_hcn_v2_1_265) show the polarized intensity map obtained at 820 nm contemporaneously with our ALMA data using VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL, as reported in Paper I.

recipe.goal: Determine stellar continuum disk center, angular size, flux density spectrum, and brightness temperature
recipe.method: Fit visibility data at line-free channels before self-calibration with a uniform elliptical disk using uvmultifit; measure integrated continuum flux densities across the 9 spectral windows and fit a frequency power law.
assumptions: Continuum is formed by optically thick free-free emission

recipe.goal: Identify spectral lines and characterize line emission/absorption morphology and kinematics
recipe.method: Cross-match detected spectral features against Splatalogue, CDMS, JPL, and HITRAN spectroscopic databases; extract spatially resolved spectra on and off the stellar disk, difference maps, and position-velocity (p-V) diagrams.
key_parameters: Five disk positions: center (pos 0) and radial offset 15 mas (0.5 R_cont) at PA = -15, 75, 165, 255 deg; off-limb positions at radii 50 mas and 90 mas; p-V slit width 5 mas at PA = 45-225 deg
assumptions: Systemic velocity V_sys = 40.4 km s^-1 LSR; partial spherical shells for p-V kinematic curves

recipe.goal: Model 30SiO v=1 and 29SiO v=3 line profiles to derive radial temperature, density, and velocity profiles
recipe.method: Construct a 1D spherical LTE radiative transfer model solving the formal integral of monochromatic intensity along lines of sight on and off the stellar continuum disk to reproduce spatially resolved spectra at positions 2 and 6.
key_parameters: Broken power-law T_gas profile (r^-3 for r <= 1.2 R_cont, r^-1 for r > 1.2 R_cont); power-law density profile r^-5 with a factor of 10 step-like drop at 1.6 R_cont; piecewise linear velocity profile from 1.0 to 2.5 R_cont
assumptions: Spherical symmetry and LTE; isotope ratio 29Si/30Si = 1; Gaussian microturbulent line profile with FWHM = 2 km s^-1; H2 density of 2.3x10^13 cm^-3 (from 3D model local density 10^-10 g cm^-3) for fractional abundance

recipe.goal: Estimate SO2 and SO excitation temperatures, column densities, and fractional abundances
recipe.method: Perform an LTE population diagram analysis on 6 thermal SO2 lines integrated in two annular regions (30–60 mas and 60–100 mas); derive SO column density from the 251.826 GHz SO line adopting the SO2 excitation temperatures.
key_parameters: SO2 lines #8, #12, #13, #19, #22, #26; inner annulus 30–60 mas, intermediate annulus 60–100 mas; SO line #41
assumptions: LTE and optically thin emission; 10% absolute flux calibration uncertainty; H2 column densities of 2.8x10^25–2.8x10^26 cm^-2 (inner) and 1.6x10^25–1.6x10^26 cm^-2 (intermediate) from r^-2 density profile based on Bladh et al. (2019)

recipe.goal: Compare spatial distributions of molecular line emission with contemporaneous visible dust-scattered polarized light
recipe.method: Create integrated intensity maps (and stacked TiO2 map) of molecular lines and overlay with the 820 nm VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL polarized intensity map from Paper I.
key_parameters: Lines compared with 820 nm polarized intensity: HCN v2=1^1e, AlO, TiO, 30SiO v=1, Si17O v=0, stacked TiO2 (lines #51-#55), SO (#41), and SO2 (lines #9, #20)

answer_key.quantity: Number of detected lines showing nonthermal emission over the stellar disk

evidence.quote: While 38 of the detected lines appear in absorption against the continuum stellar disk as expected, we detect nonthermal emission on top of the continuum over the stellar disk in 19 lines, including SiO, H$_2$O, SO$_{2}$, and AlO.

answer_key.quantity: Peak intensity of 29SiO v=2 J=6-5 maser

evidence.quote: The channel maps of the continuum-subtracted images, shown in Fig. [10](#channelmap_29sio_253), reveal three major maser clouds in the east, NNW, and WSW, where the peak intensity reaches $\sim$18 Jy/beam at $V_{\rm rel}$ = $-1.5$ to 0 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Peak brightness temperature of 29SiO v=2 J=6-5 maser

evidence.quote: The peak intensity of 18 Jy/beam corresponds to a brightness temperature of $10^6$ K.

answer_key.quantity: Model maximum infall velocity (at 1.7 R_cont = 2.5 R_*)

evidence.quote: The derived velocity profile (Fig. [8](#linemodelplot)e) shows an accelerating infall toward the star, starting from 0 km s$^{-1}$ at 2.5 $R_{\rm cont}$ (3.6 $R_{\star}$) and reaching $\sim$11 km s$^{-1}$ at 1.7 $R_{\rm cont}$ (2.5 $R_{\star}$).

answer_key.quantity: Model maximum outflow velocity at deepest layer (1 R_cont)

evidence.quote: The outflow motion becomes stronger at smaller radii and reaches $V = -10$ km s$^{-1}$ at the deepest layer.

answer_key.quantity: Model 29SiO and 30SiO number density at 1 R_cont

evidence.quote: A $^{29}$SiO (and $^{30}$SiO) number density of $\sim 5\times10^6$ cm$^{-3}$ at 1 $R_{\rm cont}$ is needed so that the blue part of the lines becomes optically thick as explained above.

answer_key.quantity: Step-like decrease factor in SiO number density at 1.6 R_cont

evidence.quote: We found it necessary to introduce a step-like decrease in the SiO number density by a factor of 10 at 1.6 $R_{\rm cont}$ to reproduce the observed $^{30}$SiO $\varv=1$ line
Our modeling suggests the change in the SiO number density by a factor of $10 \pm 5$.

answer_key.quantity: Estimated total fractional SiO abundance at 1 R_cont

evidence.quote: the (total) SiO abundance is expected to be $\ensuremath{\gtrsim} 2.2 \times 10^{-6}$.

answer_key.quantity: SO2 excitation temperature in innermost region (30–60 mas)

The uncertainties in the $T_{\rm ex}$ and $N_{\rm so_2}$ are $\pm$100 K and 46% in the inner region and $\pm$90 K and 42% in the intermediate region, respectively.

score_reason: Calibration, self-calibration intervals, CASA version, imaging parameters (pixel size, robust, multiscale scales, small-scale bias), and spectral line lists are very thoroughly documented.
